title: Outlook: usage display for Recoverable Items storage
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned display, roadmap scope and existing PowerShell controls, and appropriately leaves feature-specific licensing and defaults unknown. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting Microsoft portal guidance, qualify the quota figures for archive-enabled mailboxes, and cover the additional checks in the controls table.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Microsoft plans an Outlook display showing how much storage the user's Recoverable Items use.
claims.quote: You'll be able to see how much storage your recoverable items are using in Outlook.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes clearer storage visibility before a limit is reached to inform mailbox-management decisions.
claims.quote: This gives you a clearer picture of your storage usage before you reach a limit. You can use this information to make more informed decisions about managing your mailbox.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: February CY2027 is the roadmap target, not a committed release date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "February CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) is the only cloud listed; the record lists no US Government cloud.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The listed Outlook platforms are Desktop and Web.
claims.quote: "products": ["Outlook"], "platforms": ["Desktop", "Web"]

claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 11 November 2026 at 00:56:01.
The display's default state is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook "Recoverable Items" "usage" "display" default license. Opened: Recoverable Items folder in Exchange Online; Get-MailboxFolderStatistics; quota article. No feature-specific default found; roadmap also gives none.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Feature-specific licensing is not yet published, and the roadmap names no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook "Recoverable Items" "storage" "licensing" "usage". Opened: Recoverable Items folder in Exchange Online; quota article. Results concerned existing archiving and retention, not this display; roadmap names no licence.

claims.claim: No feature-specific price or meter is published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook recoverable items storage usage display enable disable PowerShell policy license price meter. Opened: Recoverable Items folder in Exchange Online; quota article; Get-MailboxFolderStatistics. No display-specific price or meter found.

claims.where: What's changing; front matter: changes and licensing
claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page describing the new display was found at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook "Recoverable Items" "storage" "579190" display admin setting default licensing; Outlook "Recoverable Items" "usage" "display" default license. Opened: cited Recoverable Items, cleanup, quota and cmdlet pages; none describes the new display.

claims.claim: The location of the new figure within Outlook is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook "Recoverable Items" "storage" "display" "archive" subfolders. Opened: Recoverable Items folder in Exchange Online; cleanup article; quota article. No display navigation found; roadmap gives none.

claims.claim: Whether the new display includes the archive mailbox is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook "Recoverable Items" "storage" "display" "archive" subfolders. Opened: Recoverable Items folder in Exchange Online; cleanup article; quota article. Existing archive behaviour is documented, but the display's archive coverage is not.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The display's subfolder coverage, item-name detail and calculation method are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook "Recoverable Items" "storage" "display" "archive" subfolders. Opened: Recoverable Items folder in Exchange Online; Get-MailboxFolderStatistics; quota article. No new-display subfolder, item-name or size-calculation specification found.

claims.claim: The roadmap names no permission, role, administrative visibility control, rollout mechanics or prerequisites.
claims.quote: You'll be able to see how much storage your recoverable items are using in Outlook. This gives you a clearer picture of your storage usage before you reach a limit.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap describes visibility rather than a new cleanup action or new content access.
claims.quote: You'll be able to see how much storage your recoverable items are using in Outlook.

claims.claim: No tenant admin UI or API setting governing whether the new display is shown is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook recoverable items storage usage display enable disable PowerShell policy license price meter. Opened: Get-MailboxFolderStatistics; Recoverable Items folder in Exchange Online; quota article. No display switch on either surface found.

claims.claim: No admin UI for checking Recoverable Items size by individual folder is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Exchange admin center view Recoverable Items folder size per folder user interface. Read results: Get Recoverable Items folder statistics; Exchange Mailbox usage report. The former excludes EAC; the latter reports an aggregate, not per-folder sizes.

claims.claim: Get-MailboxFolderStatistics -Identity <mailbox> -FolderScope RecoverableItems retrieves the mailbox's Recoverable Items folder statistics.
claims.quote: RecoverableItems: Returns output for the Recoverable Items folder and the Deletions, DiscoveryHolds, Purges, and Versions subfolders.

claims.claim: Learn recommends Get-EXOMailboxFolderStatistics instead in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: In Exchange Online PowerShell, we recommend that you use the Get-EXOMailboxFolderStatistics cmdlet instead of this cmdlet.

claims.claim: The -Archive switch selects statistics for the archive mailbox.
claims.quote: The Archive switch specifies whether to return the usage statistics of the archive associated with the mailbox or mail user.

claims.claim: The cited quota article gives Exchange admin center > Compliance management > Retention policies for creating the policy containing the Recoverable Items tag.
claims.quote: In the EAC, go to Compliance management > Retention policies, and then select Add
claims.fix: Acknowledge the documentation conflict: this article gives the EAC path, while https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/security-and-compliance/recoverable-items-folder/recoverable-items-folder says Exchange security and compliance features are no longer available in the new EAC. Do not present the old path as unqualified current-portal guidance.

claims.claim: The printed New-RetentionPolicyTag call creates a RecoverableItems tag with the chosen age and MoveToArchive action in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: New-RetentionPolicyTag -Name <Name of RPT> -Type RecoverableItems -AgeLimitForRetention <Number of days> -RetentionAction MoveToArchive

claims.claim: The Recoverable Items retention tag itself must be created with PowerShell, not EAC.
claims.quote: Use PowerShell to create an RPT for the Recoverable Items folder. You can't use the Exchange admin center (EAC).

claims.claim: Moving aged Recoverable Items to the archive requires an enabled archive mailbox; without it no action is taken.
claims.quote: For this process to work, the user's archive mailbox must be enabled. If the archive mailbox isn't enabled, no action is taken

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls; Why it matters
claims.claim: The documented archive and retention-tag procedure is an existing control for mailboxes on hold.
claims.quote: The rest of this article describes the step-by-step procedures to create a custom Exchange retention policy for mailboxes on hold.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said that these existing Exchange controls change the contents or calculation of the new display.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook recoverable items storage usage display enable disable PowerShell policy license price meter; Outlook "Recoverable Items" "storage" "display" "archive" subfolders. Opened: cmdlet, Recoverable Items and quota articles; none specifies control of the new display.

claims.claim: Recoverable Items resides in the mailbox's non-IPM subtree, which is not visible in Outlook clients.
claims.quote: The Recoverable Items folder resides in the non-IPM subtree of each mailbox. This subtree isn't visible to users using Outlook, Outlook on the web (formerly known as Outlook Web App), or other email clients.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Soft-deleted items are kept in Recoverable Items.
claims.quote: Soft-deleted items are moved to the Deletions subfolder of the Recoverable Items folder.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Recoverable Items preserves pre-modification copies when the relevant hold or retention policy is enabled.
claims.quote: Versions: If In-Place Hold, Litigation Hold, or a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 retention policy is enabled, this subfolder contains the original copy of the item; and also, if the item is modified multiple times, a copy of the item before modification is saved.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Hard-deleted items can be preserved in Recoverable Items by a hold or retention policy.
claims.quote: DiscoveryHolds: Contains hard-deleted items that have been preserved by an eDiscovery hold or a retention policy.

claims.claim: The listed recovery, hold, retention, mailbox-audit and calendar-logging features use Recoverable Items.
claims.quote: The following Exchange features use the Recoverable Items folder: Deleted item retention; Single item recovery; In-Place Hold; Litigation Hold; eDiscovery hold; Microsoft 365 and Office 365 retention policies; Mailbox audit logging; Calendar logging

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Purges and Versions are not visible to end users.
claims.quote: Versions: ... This folder isn't visible to end users. Purges: If either Litigation Hold or single item recovery is enabled, this subfolder contains all items that are hard deleted. This folder isn't visible to end users.

claims.claim: In-Place Hold or Litigation Hold stops automatic Managed Folder Assistant purging of DiscoveryHolds, Deletions and Purges.
claims.quote: Putting a mailbox on In-Place Hold or Litigation Hold stops the Managed Folder Assistant from automatically purging messages from the DiscoveryHolds, Deletions, and Purges subfolders.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: At the Recoverable Items quota users cannot delete items and the Managed Folder Assistant cannot delete based on retention tags.
claims.quote: Mailbox users can't delete items. The Managed Folder Assistant can't delete items based on retention tag or managed folder settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Learn advises assessing quota consumption with FolderSize rather than FolderAndSubfolderSize.
claims.quote: When you evaluate Recoverable Items folder consumption, use the FolderSize value for each Recoverable Items folder returned by Get-MailboxFolderStatistics. Don't rely on FolderAndSubfolderSize

claims.claim: An item's size is deducted from the mailbox quota and added to Recoverable Items when it moves there.
claims.quote: When an item is moved to the Recoverable Items folder, its size is deducted from the mailbox quota and added to the size of the Recoverable Items folder (quota available is reduced).

claims.claim: Exchange Online's default Recoverable Items soft and hard limits are 20 GB and 30 GB.
claims.quote: In Exchange Online, the default limits for the Recoverable Items quota are: a soft limit of 20 GB and a hard limit of 30 GB.

claims.claim: Litigation Hold, In-Place Hold or a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 retention policy automatically raises the stated baseline limits to 90 GB and 100 GB.
claims.quote: the quotas for the Recoverable Items folder are automatically increased to 90 GB and 100 GB, respectively, when you place a mailbox on Litigation Hold or In-Place Hold or if a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 retention policy is applied to the mailbox.
claims.fix: Keep these baseline figures but add the same page's qualification: enabling archiving for a mailbox on hold or assigned a retention policy raises the primary mailbox's warning quota to 95 GB and storage quota to 105 GB. This matters because the briefing discusses archive configuration as a response to storage pressure.

claims.claim: Data preserved by a hold should not simply be deleted to free space.
claims.quote: If the mailbox is placed on In-Place Hold, Litigation Hold, or another type of hold in Microsoft 365 or Office 365, or if single item recovery is enabled, you'll want to preserve the mailbox data until the hold is removed or single item recovery is disabled.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The controls table covers every control the governance checklist asks administrators to inspect.
claims.quote: Identify mailboxes on Litigation Hold, In-Place Hold or a retention policy, using Exchange Online PowerShell. ... decide whether the archive mailbox and a retention policy tag ... fit your holds. The table covers only display availability, folder statistics and tag/policy creation.
claims.fix: Add rows for checking mailbox hold/retention status and archive-mailbox enablement, with researched UI/API documentation, or narrow the checklist to the controls already documented in the table. Do not use the tag-creation row as a substitute for checking archive enablement.
